one_liner: TypeScript runtime validation compiled directly from your types — no duplicate schema definitions.
description: schemaguard is a TypeScript library that generates runtime validators from your existing type declarations at build time. Instead of maintaining a Zod schema alongside every interface, you keep one source of truth: the types you already wrote. The compiler plugin emits tiny, fast validators for API boundaries, forms, and untrusted JSON.
target_user: TypeScript developers validating untrusted data at API boundaries

icp.who: TypeScript-heavy product teams with typed API contracts between services or client and server
icp.pain: Every interface gets duplicated as a hand-written Zod or Yup schema that drifts out of sync with the real types
icp.buying_trigger: A production incident caused by an API response that no longer matched the TypeScript types the client assumed

differentiators: Zero schema duplication: validators are compiled from existing TypeScript types, not written by hand
Benchmark: validates 1M objects/sec versus roughly 180k/sec for an equivalent Zod schema
proof_points: Benchmark suite in repo shows ~5.5x throughput over Zod on the same payloads
Runtime core measured at 2.1 kB gzipped
Adopted in production by three seed-stage startups named in the README

voice.sample_phrase: One source of truth: the types you already wrote.

signals: Version 0.4.x on npm, API marked unstable in docs
Breaking changes noted between minor versions
Active weekly commits, small contributor base

gaps: Webpack support still open as an issue

confidence.notes: Benchmarks and bundle size are reproducible from the repo. Production adoption claims rest on README statements.
